newsitem.title: UK: British inflation rate falls to 2.1 percent in August.
newsitem.headline: British inflation rate falls to 2.1 percent in August.

text.p: Britain's annual inflation rate fell to 2.1 percent in August from 2.2 percent in July, official figures showed on Thursday. But a 0.5 percent rise in retail prices in August, caused principally by higher petrol prices, disappointed financial markets. Retail prices had fallen 0.4 percent in July.
Food prices rose more slowly than last year, when fresh food was affected by a drought, but beef prices put upward pressure on inflation as the effects of the BSE scare began to wear off.
Analysts said the data suggested inflation had levelled out and appeared to rule out chances of a cut soon in interest rates.
"They are a little bit disappointing. They tend to rule out a rate cut or they certainly don't argue for a rate cut," said economist Peter Osler of GNI.
Sterling inched up against the mark after the figures but shares pared gains and government bonds slipped. British interest rates stand at 5.75 percent, having been cut four times since December.

The Conservative government estimates the underlying rate of inflation, which excludes monthly payments on home loans, should ease to 2.5 percent over the medium term but it has been stuck at 2.8 percent since May.

Angela Knight, economic secretary at the Treasury, said the data showed Britain's long run of sustained low inflation was continuing. The data came a day after figures showed the jobless rate fell to 7.5 percent -- a 5-1/2 year low -- in August.
